data.title: Š. Meliš: Traces of the pagan gods
data.excerpt: With the kind permission of Štefan Meliš we present his article, originally published in Historická revue no. III, volume 8. He reads the place names of the Papradno and Mariková valleys – Pernajov, Bohov, Hromovec – as traces of the worship of the gods Perún and Veles.

timeline.title: The worship of Perún at Pernajov
timeline.description: According to Š. Meliš, our ancestors here worshipped the god Perún, whom they may have called Pernaj, Perunaj.

children.text: With the kind permission of Mr Štefan Meliš we bring you his interesting article, which was originally published in Historická revue no. III, volume 8.

blocks.text:
In the village of Stupné, in the Papradno valley, there is a hill called Žeravica. On its southern side it is craggy and steep. Members of the archaeological club from Považská Bystrica identified La Tène occupation of the Roman period on it, and, judging by sherds with wavy-line decoration, Slavic occupation as well. At the end of the little valley below the southern slope of Žeravica, at the boundary between the cadastral areas of the villages of Stupné and Hvozdnica, there is a locality called Pernajov. I think that it was here that our ancestors worshipped the god Perún in the 9th–11th centuries, whom they may have called Pernaj, Perunaj. Perhaps the ending naj was understood in the sense of the prefix naj-, the highest god.
About two kilometres further south, on the boundary between the villages of Jasenica and Hvozdnica, there is another interesting hill. On the maps it is admittedly marked as Súdna, but the people of the neighbourhood call it Bohov. It was probably a place of the pagan gods, that is, a božnica, a božište, where our ancestors worshipped a whole range of other gods besides Perún.
Another, no less remarkable name is that of the hill Hromovec at Hatné, in the Mariková valley. It stands directly above the main road, and its name certainly comes from Perún, who sent thunder down to the earth. It seems that Perún was worshipped on this hill too, and that animals were perhaps even sacrificed to him here. A large pit has survived on Hromovec to this day; it is about 6–7 metres long, 4 metres wide and almost 2 metres deep. It may have been a sacrificial site.
At Papradno, it seems, a memory of the pagan god Veles has remained. Below the hill Západliská there is a small lake measuring 6 × 20 metres (below the locality of Letková), where according to legend fairies used to dance. There was once said to be murky water in it. Bľabota settled in the lake. It was a hideous apparition which had the shape of the pagan god Veles – a mighty great fellow with a cow's head. After the evening bell (“for peace”), Bľabota would come out of the little lake, walk about the village, poke its head into the windows and frighten people by babbling and in human speech. It appears that after the adoption of Christianity the previously worshipped god Veles – the protector of herds – was turned here into a hideous apparition.
